summary: AE+SE walked customer through Redwood Console tracing, request logs, and error analysis. Covered how to correlate trace IDs with request logs, use error analysis to triage model/regression issues, and configure alerting and retention. Customer interested in Dedicated for predictable latency and wants a POC/benchmark. Security docs requested.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-06-04
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood CSM); Sara Lopez (Kestrel Head of ML), Daniel Park (Kestrel CTO), Ravi Sharma (Kestrel Platform), Maya Nguyen (Kestrel SRE)
Meeting Link / Recording: https://app.fireflies.ai/rec/ff-20250604-8321

[00:00] Alex Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. Quick intro - I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and Priya will do most of the console deep-dive.
[00:11] Sara Lopez: Thanks Alex, excited to see the tracing bits, we've had trouble debugging the reranker instabilities.
[00:18] Priya Desai: Awesome, we'll focus on tracing, request logs, and how error analysis surfaces model regressions and noisy tokens. I'll share my screen.
[01:05] Priya Desai: Ok, so this is the Redwood Console home page, and you can see per-route metrics - latency, cost-per-token, error rate — quick drill into the chat-route here. 
[01:23] Daniel Park: Real quick, are these aggregated at the model level or per-deployment?
[01:28] Priya Desai: They're per-route, which maps to a model+deployment combo. You can pin to a specific deployment or view across variants. Small note, sometimes the UI auto-label shows "Redwood Control" in older accounts, ignore that if you see it.
[02:10] Priya Desai: Now tracing - each request generates a trace id that ties together the frontend request, routing decision, model invocation and downstream post-processing. You can click any span to see timings and logs.
[02:42] Ravi Sharma: Do you correlate KV cache hits? We saw big variance due to cold caches.
[02:47] Priya Desai: Yes, cache hits are a span-level tag. In the trace waterfall you'll see a KV cache hit/miss annotation (sometimes transcribed as KV cash in older logs), and you can filter traces by that tag.
[03:30] Priya Desai: Example: here's a slow request - you can see a long tokenization step (20ms) and then a stalled network to the dedicated pool - that was a routing fallback to the burst lane.
[03:46] Sara Lopez: Can we export traces to our datadog?
[03:50] Priya Desai: Absolutely, we have an export connector. We also provide a raw JSON download for each trace. I can share the doc link after.
[04:30] Alex Kim: Quick plug, we'll include the tracing connector link in the follow-up so you can wire into your existing observability.
[05:05] Priya Desai: Moving on to Request Logs - this is a search table where you can filter by trace id, user id, latency, error code, model version, and prompt hash. It's full text searchable.
[05:41] Daniel Park: How long do you retain logs by default?
[05:45] Priya Desai: Hosted default is 30 days, enterprise retention can be configured for longer - it's part of the Dedicated/Private settings.
[06:10] Priya Desai: Error analysis - this is a surfaced view that clusters errors by fingerprint. For example, we group malformed responses, timeouts, and hallucinations separately, and show top-affected routes and sample prompts.
[06:34] Maya Nguyen: How do you detect hallucinations automatically?
[06:38] Priya Desai: We use a combination of heuristic evals and customer-supplied checks — customers can supply a set of validation prompts, and the console runs those as evaluators to tag regressions. We also support metric-based anomalies.
[07:05] Sara Lopez: Can we hook in our post-processing checks? We have strict PII scrubbing rules.
[07:12] Priya Desai: Yes, you can register custom validators that run post-model. The errors will show up in the same error analysis dashboard.
[07:45] Priya Desai: I'll demo a real example: a regression where the reranker started returning empty choices after a model update.
[08:02] [08:02] Priya Desai: Here you see error cluster "empty_response", grouped by prompt-hash; clicking into a cluster shows the most recent failing traces and the code path.
[08:28] Ravi Sharma: Is the trace id present in the log file we can ship to Splunk?
[08:33] Priya Desai: Yes, trace id and request id are in the request log row and available via the export API.
[09:10] Alex Kim: happy to send the sample export payload after the call.
[09:35] Priya Desai: Now about alerting - you can create alert rules for p95 latency, error rate, or custom metric derived from evaluations. Alerts can post to Slack, PagerDuty, or call webhooks.
[09:58] Daniel Park: Do alerts include trace links?
[10:02] Priya Desai: Yes, alerts include the top offending trace link and a sample request payload.
[10:40] Priya Desai: Security and access — RBAC is available, and we support SAML/SCIM for SSO. Audit logs include request-level access for compliance.
[11:05] Sara Lopez: We'll need SOC2 artifacts and KMS integration details.
[11:10] Alex Kim: We'll attach the SOC2 pack and KMS guide in the follow-up.
[12:00] Priya Desai: Back to debugging flows — here's how you go from an alert to a RCA: click the alert, open the trace link, jump to the request log row, then run the built-in replay runner which replays the request against a pinned model version in a sandbox.
[12:43] Maya Nguyen: Replay runner sounds useful for reproducing non-deterministic failures. Does it re-run with same seed and kv cache state?
[12:52] Priya Desai: We capture the request environment but not the exact GPU RNG seed. For deterministic models you can pin seeds; for cache we simulate prefix state where possible. It's good for surface-level repro.
[13:35] Priya Desai: Now I'll show you how to filter by a user's session and then mass-export the set for a focused run.
[14:02] [14:02] Priya Desai: Filtering demo...
[15:00] Priya Desai: I also want to highlight the "Model Regression" tab in Error Analysis where you can tie regressions to model versions and quantify quality deltas using your eval set.
[15:29] Sara Lopez: Does that require us to upload a gold set?
[15:33] Priya Desai: You can upload a JSONL gold set, or use the Redwood Evaluate templates. The console will compute delta metrics and flag regressions over time.
[16:20] Daniel Park: For Dedicated, are traces routed differently? We worry about cross-tenant leakage.
[16:29] Priya Desai: Dedicated isolates telemetry at the cluster level; you still get the same Console but with private data plane. Audit logs and KMS are also available.
[17:01] Ravi Sharma: Latency targets — what's realistic for 512 tokens?
[17:06] Priya Desai: On Dedicated small-batch 512 tokens p95 is usually sub-100ms on our optimized runtime for certain models. We'll need your traffic profile for precise numbers.
[17:28] Alex Kim: We'll run a benchmark as part of the POC using your sample traffic.
[17:40] Priya Desai: Quick note, streaming traces show per-token timing so you can see when generation starts to stall.
[18:05] Sara Lopez: Can we set different retention for traces vs logs?
[18:09] Priya Desai: Yes, retention is configurable per artifact type.
[18:50] Priya Desai: Let's demo a live triage - I'm going to trigger a synthetic failing request.
[19:12] [19:12] Priya Desai: (typing) sending request...okay it's registered, you can see the trace id - 0x3a5f2b.
[19:35] Maya Nguyen: I see it, the waterfall shows a long gen span.
[19:40] Priya Desai: Expand the span - generator shows repeated retries; the model backend returned 503 on two attempts which the router then retried to a fallback variant.
[20:05] Daniel Park: Is retry logic configurable? We prefer failing fast for some flows.
[20:10] Priya Desai: Retry policy is configurable per-route; you can choose fail-fast or aggressive retry.
[20:45] Priya Desai: For debugging, you can also annotate traces and add notes for runbooks which are then surfaced in the RCA timeline.
[21:20] Alex Kim: Any questions on the tracing flow?
[21:25] Sara Lopez: One thing — can we mask PII in logs before they hit the Console?
[21:30] Priya Desai: Yes, Redwood can apply pre-ingest scrubbing rules in the edge. For Private deployments you can run scrubbing in your VPC.
[22:05] Priya Desai: Another feature is request sampling - you can increase sampling on certain user segments so you don't blow up storage.
[22:30] Ravi Sharma: For benchmarks we'll want full fidelity for a subset though.
[22:35] Priya Desai: Totally — you can configure full-fidelity capture for tagged routes.
[23:10] Priya Desai: Now request logs exports - here's the export config. You can schedule daily exports to S3 or push to your SIEM.
[23:35] Daniel Park: Any cost to longer retention?
[23:39] Priya Desai: Retention beyond defaults is bundled into Dedicated pricing, or as an add-on for hosted customers. We'll share the SKU in the follow-up.
[24:10] Priya Desai: Quick live query: filter by error code 502 and model v1.2 - we get 24 hits in the last 24 hours.
[24:35] [24:35] Priya Desai: opening a log row — here you can see request payload, model response, latency, and a direct link to the associated trace.
[25:12] Sara Lopez: Could we ingest these logs into our ML monitoring tool for drift detection?
[25:18] Priya Desai: Yes — we have an API and webhooks that push payloads for custom downstream analysis.
[25:45] Priya Desai: A note about mis-transcriptions — sometimes the automatic speaker labels are off, you'll see Speaker 1/2 in older transcripts.
[26:10] Alex Kim: Great callout — our recorded transcripts include timestamped speaker segments but not perfect.
[26:50] Priya Desai: Next, we'll step through the error analysis regression UI — here you can drill from a spike in hallucination rate down to specific prompts and then open a batch re-run to validate against a control model.
[27:20] Priya Desai: The batch re-run can be scoped to a time window and will produce a delta report visible in the console.
[28:00] Sara Lopez: That delta report — can it be exported as CSV for stakeholders?
[28:04] Priya Desai: Yes, CSV export and a shareable report link.
[28:40] Daniel Park: For the POC we'll need the raw request + response pairs for 1000 examples. Is that possible?
[28:46] Priya Desai: Yes, we can provide an export. We'll need to ensure any PII is scrubbed if you request it.
[29:10] Priya Desai: Going to the routing page now — you can set policies to prioritize latency, cost, or regional routing. If Dedicated is unavailable, you can fall back to hosted variants.
[29:38] Ravi Sharma: How do fallbacks affect trace continuity?
[29:42] Priya Desai: The trace will show the routing step and the fallback decision; you can filter for traces that encountered fallbacks.
[30:05] Priya Desai: I'm going to show the alerting rule create flow — set metric, threshold, notification, and attach a runbook.
[30:40] [30:40] Priya Desai: (creating rule)... done. This will hit Slack and include a consolidated link to the top 5 traces.
[31:10] Maya Nguyen: Does the alert include a snapshot of recent request logs?
[31:15] Priya Desai: It includes a sample that you can click to expand.
[31:40] Alex Kim: Quick reminder — we'll send the SOC2 doc and the KMS integration whitepaper right after.
[32:00] Sara Lopez: Request: can we get a cost estimate for 5M tokens/month with 30-day retention and increased trace retention?
[32:08] Alex Kim: We'll include that in the pricing sheet.
[32:45] Priya Desai: A couple of gotchas — when you do heavy tracing and full-fidelity capture it increases storage cost; recommended is targeted capture for high-value routes.
[33:12] Daniel Park: For model regressions, how do you prevent false positives from post-processing changes?
[33:18] Priya Desai: You can pin the post-processing pipeline version in the evaluation so comparisons are apples-to-apples.
[33:55] Priya Desai: Now I'll show the replay runner configuration — choose a target model version, toggle environment variables, and run in a sandbox.
[34:20] [34:20] Priya Desai: running replay... results populate in a few seconds... here's the diff between control and candidate.
[34:45] Sara Lopez: Useful. We'll need to run this against our reranker and downstream features.
[35:00] Alex Kim: We typically do a week-long bench with customers to measure p95 and cost per request.
[35:20] Priya Desai: Onboarding checklist: share sample traffic, set retention requirements, request SOC2/KMS docs, schedule bench.
[35:42] Priya Desai: I'll drop links to the Console help pages in chat now (tracing guide, error-analysis, export APIs).
[36:05] [36:05] Priya Desai: chat: https://redwood.ai/docs/console/tracing (note: link for demo)
[36:40] Daniel Park: One more question — can we run Private (on-prem) with the same Console experience?
[36:47] Priya Desai: Yes, Private offers the same control plane UI but you host the data plane. There are a few network and KMS differences; we document them in the Private deployment guide.
[37:20] Ravi Sharma: For Private we need offline upgrade processes and air-gapped install docs.
[37:26] Priya Desai: We have an on-prem package and partner-run installs; I'll share the air-gap checklist.
[38:00] Priya Desai: Quick demo of the RCA timeline — here's an incident, you can see annotations from SRE, linked traces, and the postmortem artifact.
[38:30] Maya Nguyen: Nice, that would fit our incident workflow.
[39:05] Priya Desai: We also have throttles and circuit-breaker visualizations so you can see when the router tripped and which tenant was impacted.
[39:40] Sara Lopez: Do you keep a long-term history for audits?
[39:44] Priya Desai: Audit retention is configurable; we can align with your compliance window as part of Dedicated.
[40:10] Alex Kim: Wrapping up, any final blockers?
[40:15] Daniel Park: Just timing—need to align on pilot scope and sign-off from security.
[40:20] Sara Lopez: Also need to validate that PII scrubbing will meet our lawyers' requirements.
[40:30] Alex Kim: Understood. We'll send the SOC2 pack and the KMS + scrubbing guide.
[41:05] Priya Desai: Last demo piece — alerting runbook integration and scheduled exports.
[41:35] Priya Desai: (demo) done — that's the end of the interactive section.
[42:00] Alex Kim: Next steps recap — we'll send pricing, SOC2, KMS, tracing docs, and propose bench dates.
[42:15] Sara Lopez: Sounds good.
[42:20] Daniel Park: We'll try to get traffic profiles by 2025-06-09.
[42:25] Ravi Sharma: I'll pull a 7 day sample and scrub PII before sending.
[42:35] Alex Kim: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up by EOD 2025-06-05 with the sheet.
[42:50] Priya Desai: Thanks all — happy to schedule the infra deep dive next week.
[43:10] Meeting end / recording stopped.
